newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Refoundation to follow own line on welfare.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Refoundation to follow own line on welfare.

text.p: Italy's hard-line Communist Refoundation party said on Tuesday that it would stick to its own line in negotiations between the centre-left government, unions and employers over welfare reform.
"Tomorrow talks between the government and the social parties on reform of the welfare state will begin," said Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti in a statement.
"We would have preferred it to have been preceded by the definition of a common position by the (centre-left) majority on a decisive issue for the country.
"That did not happen. The government decided otherwise and therefore its positions do not bind the entire majority."

Bertinotti said Refoundation would work towards ensuring what he called "a good reform of the welfare state by introducing a new policy for employment and avoiding any cut in social spending and pensions".

Refoundation agrees that Italy's welfare state has to be reformed but say any changes should not involve a cut to overall spending. Many economists have called for an overhaul of the costly pension system to keep state accounts in order.

Communist Refoundation lies outside the government coalition but guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament. The party has threatened to bring down Prime Minister Romano Prodi if he tries to cut back on social spending.
